title: Instrumentation Probe Orchestrator: unified sampling & async-safe tracing hooks
creator: Aisha Romero
description: Scope: Build a lightweight 'probe orchestrator' library for Redwood SDKs and middleware that centralizes sampling decisions, exposes async-safe tracing hooks, and gracefully bridges legacy clients. Goals: 1) Ensure deterministic sampling hints propagate across async boundaries (workers, queues, websockets) without adding significant latency; 2) Provide a unified hook surface for non-blocking span creation and enrichment used by the Console and metrics pipeline; 3) Offer a fall-back path for older SDKs and third-party frameworks; 4) Integrate with the metrics/log pipelines so span attributes can be correlated with logs and metrics at ingest time. Deliverables: design doc, core library (TS/Go/Py interfaces), integration tests exercising cross-process propagation, a canary rollout plan for the hosted API, and perf/latency targets (<=0.5ms median overhead on hot paths, P99 < 5ms).
background: We currently have multiple tracing shims implemented across SDKs and edge components (ad-hoc hooks, header rewriters, and context carriers). This has led to inconsistent sampling behavior when requests traverse async boundaries (e.g., websocket pings -> background workers) and duplicated sampling logic in each SDK. Console dashboards show spikes of sampling mismatch between traces and metrics during burst traffic. A unified orchestrator would reduce duplication, improve sampling signal quality for alerts, and simplify future additions (e.g., signed provenance header).
qa_checklist: 1) Unit tests for propagation across Promise/async/threads; 2) Integration tests with edge-proxy and worker queue (local harness); 3) Load test at 5k RPS with sampling=5% and verify trace/metric alignment; 4) Smoke canary in us-west-2 for 48h; 5) Verify Console latency dashboard shows <1% regression in tail latency.
migration_plan: Phase 1: ship probe-orch library as opt-in SDK dependency and enable for internal services only. Phase 2: enable for hosted API traffic with sampling hints off by default and a 1% controlled rollout. Phase 3: flip default sampling propagation for all SDKs after 2 weeks of stable metrics. Provide rollback flag and graceful header ignore mode for incompatible clients.
risks: - Backward compatibility: some older clients don't support new header format; mitigated by dual-write of legacy headers. - Latency: adding orchestration on hot paths may add overhead; mitigated by microbenchmarks and fast-path bypass when sampling not required. - Operator error during rollout: mitigate with phased canaries and feature flags.
performance_targets: median overhead <= 0.5ms on request-critical path; P95 < 2ms; P99 < 5ms under typical workloads (1-2k RPS per instance).
rollout_plan: 1) Internal infra services (1% of traffic) - 3 days smoke. 2) Developer sandbox orgs - 2 days. 3) Hosted API canary us-west-2 - 48h at 0.5% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% if stable. 4) Promote to Dedicated tenants as opt-in through console toggle.
